claim: The study reports the entire synaptic connectome of glomerulus VA1v of the right antennal lobe in Drosophila melanogaster using FIB-SEM.
source: Using FIB-SEM we report the entire synaptic connectome of glomerulus VA1v of the right antennal lobe in Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: The abstract directly states this as the main finding of the study.

claim: All neurons within glomerulus VA1v were densely reconstructed, including local interneurons.
source: Within the glomerulus we densely reconstructed all neurons, including hitherto elusive local interneurons.
evidence: The abstract states that dense reconstruction was performed on all neurons.

claim: VA1v is a fruitless-positive, sexually dimorphic glomerulus.
source: The fruitless-positive, sexually dimorphic VA1v included >11,140 presynaptic sites with ~38,050 postsynaptic dendrites.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes VA1v as fruitless-positive and sexually dimorphic.

claim: VA1v contains more than 11,140 presynaptic sites with approximately 38,050 postsynaptic dendrites.
source: The fruitless-positive, sexually dimorphic VA1v included >11,140 presynaptic sites with ~38,050 postsynaptic dendrites.
evidence: The abstract provides specific quantitative data from the reconstruction.

claim: VA1v is innervated by 51 ipsilateral and 56 contralateral olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs).
source: These connected input olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs, 51 ipsilateral, 56 contralateral), output projection neurons (18 PNs), and local interneurons (56 of >150 previously reported LNs).
evidence: The abstract provides specific counts of ORNs from the reconstruction.

claim: VA1v contains 18 projection neurons (PNs).
source: These connected input olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs, 51 ipsilateral, 56 contralateral), output projection neurons (18 PNs), and local interneurons (56 of >150 previously reported LNs).
evidence: The abstract provides the specific count of PNs identified.

claim: VA1v contains 56 local interneurons (LNs) out of more than 150 previously reported for the entire antennal lobe.
source: These connected input olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs, 51 ipsilateral, 56 contralateral), output projection neurons (18 PNs), and local interneurons (56 of >150 previously reported LNs).
evidence: The abstract provides the count of LNs in VA1v and references previous reports.

claim: ORNs are predominantly presynaptic in VA1v.
source: ORNs are predominantly presynaptic and PNs predominantly postsynaptic
evidence: The abstract characterizes the synaptic polarity of ORNs.

claim: PNs are predominantly postsynaptic in VA1v.
source: ORNs are predominantly presynaptic and PNs predominantly postsynaptic
evidence: The abstract characterizes the synaptic polarity of PNs.

claim: LN circuits are largely an equal mixture of pre- and postsynaptic contacts and confer extensive synaptic reciprocity.
source: newly reported LN circuits are largely an equal mixture and confer extensive synaptic reciprocity, except the newly reported LN2V with input from ORNs and outputs mostly to monoglomerular PNs, however.
evidence: The abstract describes the synaptic characteristics of LN circuits.

claim: LN2V is an exception among LNs, receiving input from ORNs and providing outputs mostly to monoglomerular PNs.
source: newly reported LN circuits are largely an equal mixture and confer extensive synaptic reciprocity, except the newly reported LN2V with input from ORNs and outputs mostly to monoglomerular PNs, however.
evidence: The abstract specifically identifies LN2V as having distinct connectivity patterns.

claim: PNs were more numerous than previously reported from genetic screens.
source: PNs were more numerous than previously reported from genetic screens, suggesting that the latter failed to reach saturation.
evidence: The abstract compares the current findings with previous genetic screen results.

claim: Genetic screens for PNs failed to reach saturation.
source: PNs were more numerous than previously reported from genetic screens, suggesting that the latter failed to reach saturation.
evidence: The abstract infers this conclusion from the discrepancy in PN numbers.

claim: A matrix of 192 neuron bodies each having more than 50 connections was reported.
source: We report a matrix of 192 bodies each having >50 connections; these form 88% of the glomerulus' pre/postsynaptic sites.
evidence: The abstract provides specific quantitative data about the connectivity matrix.

claim: The 192 neuron bodies with more than 50 connections form 88% of the glomerulus' pre/postsynaptic sites.
source: We report a matrix of 192 bodies each having >50 connections; these form 88% of the glomerulus' pre/postsynaptic sites.
evidence: The abstract provides the percentage of synaptic sites accounted for by these neurons.

claim: Advanced brains in insects and mammals show close similarities in structures that analyze olfactory information.
source: A striking convergence in advanced brains has endowed those structures of the brains in insects and mammals that analyse olfactory information with close similarities (Hildebrand and Shepherd, 1997).
evidence: The introduction cites a reference supporting this comparative statement.

claim: In both insects and mammals, segregated modules of neuropile called glomeruli receive input from olfactory receptor neuron axons.
source: In both, segregated modules of neuropile called glomeruli each receive input from the axons of olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs), each of which in turn expresses predominantly a single olfactory receptor gene (Gao et al., 2000; Vosshall et al., 2000).
evidence: The introduction describes the common organization with citations.

claim: Each ORN predominantly expresses a single olfactory receptor gene.
source: In both, segregated modules of neuropile called glomeruli each receive input from the axons of olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs), each of which in turn expresses predominantly a single olfactory receptor gene (Gao et al., 2000; Vosshall et al., 2000).
evidence: The introduction states this with supporting citations.

claim: ORNs in adult Drosophila melanogaster belong to one of four classes of sensilla on the third antennal segment and maxillary palp.
source: ORNs in the adult fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster belong to one of four classes of sensilla that form a regular pattern on the third segment of the fly's antenna and maxillary palp (Vosshall and Stocker, 2007).
evidence: The introduction describes ORN organization with a citation.

claim: The mouse olfactory bulb contains approximately 5 million ORNs that innervate approximately 1800 glomeruli.
source: Compared with the ~5×106 ORNs (Kawagishi et al., 2014) that innervate the ~1800 glomeruli in the mouse olfactory bulb (Royet et al., 1988)
evidence: The introduction provides quantitative comparison with citations.

claim: Drosophila has 1300 ORNs that express 62 odorant receptor proteins.
source: Thus, only 1300 ORNs that express 62 odorant receptor proteins (Vosshall and Stocker, 2007)
evidence: The introduction provides specific numbers with a citation.

claim: Drosophila ORNs innervate approximately 50 modular glomeruli.
source: innervate a mere ~50 modular glomeruli (Grabe et al., 2015), the first relay of the insect olfactory system (Stocker, 1994; Laissue et al., 1999; Gao et al., 2000; Vosshall et al., 2000; Benton et al., 2009; Grabe et al., 2015).
evidence: The introduction states this with supporting citations.

claim: Glomeruli are the first relay of the insect olfactory system.
source: innervate a mere ~50 modular glomeruli (Grabe et al., 2015), the first relay of the insect olfactory system (Stocker, 1994; Laissue et al., 1999; Gao et al., 2000; Vosshall et al., 2000; Benton et al., 2009; Grabe et al., 2015).
evidence: The introduction describes the functional role with citations.

claim: Each of the approximately 50 glomeruli has been individually identified and mapped.
source: Each of the ~50 glomeruli has been individually identified (Laissue et al., 1999; Benton et al., 2009; Silbering et al., 2011) and mapped, both in vitro, after dissection (Stocker et al., 1983; Laissue et al., 1999; Couto et al., 2005; Endo et al., 2007); Silbering et al., 2011) and in vivo (Grabe et al., 2015).
evidence: The introduction describes previous mapping work with multiple citations.

claim: Projection neurons (PNs) relay olfactory information from glomeruli to the mushroom body and lateral horn.
source: Output from the glomeruli is made by the antennal lobe projection neurons (PNs), some of which relay olfactory information to higher-order olfactory centres, the mushroom body and lateral horn (Wong et al., 2002; Marin et al., 2002; Yasuyama et al., 2002; Yasuyama et al., 2003)
evidence: The introduction describes PN function with citations.

claim: PNs project via three main antennal lobe tracts: medial (mALT), mediolateral (mlALT), and lateral (lALT).
source: via three main antennal lobe tracts (ALTs), medial, mediolateral and lateral (mALT, mlALT and lALT).
evidence: The introduction describes the anatomical organization of PN projections.

claim: Tanaka et al. (2012) identified eleven classes of PNs: four in the medial, three in the mediolateral, and four in the lateral tracts.
source: Among the PNs, Tanaka et al. (2012) have identified eleven classes, four in the medial, three in the mediolateral, and four in the lateral tracts.
evidence: The introduction cites specific classification from Tanaka et al. 2012.

claim: mPN1s project from the antennal lobe along the mALT to the mushroom body and lateral horn.
source: Amongst these, mPN1s project out of the antennal lobe along the mALT to the mushroom body and lateral horn (Tanaka et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction describes mPN1 projections with a citation.

claim: ORNs have been morphologically less well characterized than PNs but are recently catalogued for glomerulus DM6.
source: Relative to these, ORNs have been morphologically less well characterized but are recently catalogued for glomerulus DM6 (Tobin et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction compares the state of knowledge with a citation.

claim: Tanaka identified LNs of six types with cell bodies in different locations.
source: Tanaka has identified LNs of six types with cell bodies in different locations, which arborize in either single or multiple glomeruli and in the antennal lobe of either one or both sides (Table 1).
evidence: The introduction references Tanaka's classification of LNs.

claim: Chou et al. (2010) identify at least approximately 100 different LNs for each side of the antennal lobe.
source: Categorized by the glomeruli they innervate, Chou et al. (2010) identify at least ~100 different LNs for each side.
evidence: The introduction cites specific LN counts from Chou et al. 2010.

claim: Additional cell types in the antennal lobe include a single 5-HT neuron and several transverse (tALT) neurons.
source: Additional cell types identified include a single 5-HT neuron and several transverse (tALT) neurons (Tanaka et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction lists additional cell types with a citation.

claim: Fluorescent pre- and postsynaptic markers provide proxies for claimed synaptic contacts but lack independent validation from EM.
source: Fluorescent pre- and postsynaptic markers provide proxies for claimed synaptic contacts (Mosca and Luo, 2014), but lack independent validation from EM.
evidence: The introduction critiques fluorescent marker approaches with a citation.

claim: Rybak et al. (2016) studied three glomeruli (DL5, DM2, and VA7) and provided a map of synaptic connections and their numerical proportions.
source: Two recent studies (Rybak et al., 2016; Tobin et al., 2017) report the synaptic networks of identified glomeruli. The first, a study of three glomeruli (DL5, DM2, and VA7: Laissue et al., 1999), has provided a significant map of synaptic connections and their numerical proportions
evidence: The introduction describes previous EM studies with citations.

claim: Tobin et al. (2017) studied glomerulus DM6 and established many features of the PN.
source: while the second, on glomerulus DM6 (Tobin et al., 2017), established many features of the PN.
evidence: The introduction describes a previous study with a citation.

claim: Neither Rybak et al. (2016) nor Tobin et al. (2017) gave a comprehensive account of the varied synaptic inputs from and between LNs.
source: Neither study gave a comprehensive account of the varied synaptic inputs from and between LNs, however.
evidence: The introduction identifies a gap in previous studies.

claim: The study used an isotropic 8 nm voxel image stack obtained by focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM).
source: We report the connectome of a single glomerulus VA1v of the right side of a female Drosophila antennal lobe (Figure 1), using dense reconstruction of an isotropic 8 nm voxel image stack (Figure 2), see Materials and methods, obtained by focused ion beam (FIB) milling scanning electron microscopy, FIB-SEM (Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: The Results section describes the imaging method with a citation.

claim: VA1v is responsive to fly odour.
source: VA1v is a sexually dimorphic fruitless-positive glomerulus responsive to fly odour (Sakurai et al., 2013)
evidence: The Results section describes VA1v function with a citation.

claim: VA1v signals the sex pheromones cis-vaccenyl acetate and methyl laurate.
source: that signals the sex pheromones cis-vaccenyl acetate and methyl laurate (Kurtovic et al., 2007; Dweck et al., 2013)
evidence: The Results section describes VA1v function with citations.

claim: VA1v is significantly larger in male flies than in females.
source: and is significantly larger in male flies than in females (Kondoh et al., 2003; Stockinger et al., 2005).
evidence: The Results section describes sexual dimorphism with citations.

source: Each synapse comprised a T-bar ribbon at the presynaptic site opposite membrane densities at the postsynaptic dendrites (Figure 3A).

source: LN1 and LN2L 3.17 and 3.06 respectively

source: Occasional synapses were bidirectional, with a T-bar ribbon on either side of the synaptic cleft.

claim: The volumetric packing density of synapses in VA1v (one site per 2.29 µm³) corresponds approximately to values reported from TEM by Rybak et al. (2016) for glomerulus VA7.
source: The volumetric packing density of synapses, one site per 2.29 µm3 of neuropile, corresponds approximately to the differently computed values reported from TEM by Rybak et al. (2016) for glomerulus VA7
evidence: The Discussion section compares synapse density with a previous study.

claim: The synapse density in VA1v is less than the density of synapses in the first and second optic neuropiles, the lamina and medulla.
source: but is less than the density of synapses in the first and second optic neuropiles, the lamina and medulla (Meinertzhagen, 2014).
evidence: The Discussion section compares synapse density across brain regions with a citation.

claim: The study provides the complete connectome from a sensory neuropile in Drosophila.
source: We provide the complete connectome from a sensory neuropile in Drosophila
evidence: The Discussion section characterizes the scope of the study.

claim: The VA1v connectome lacks most of the circuits of the approximately 50 other glomeruli to which most multiglomerular local interneurons also extend.
source: Like the latter, for all it is comprehensive the connectome of this single fruitless-positive glomerulus lacks most of the circuits of any of the approximately 50 other glomeruli, even of its neighbours, to which most of the local interneurons, those that are multiglomerular, also extend.
evidence: The Discussion section acknowledges limitations of studying a single glomerulus.

claim: The mostly complete agreement between FIB-EM and Gal4 enhancer-trap labels provides assurance that both methods reliably succeed in identifying cell types of glomerulus VA1v.
source: The mostly complete agreement we find between the two methods, reported here for FIB-EM and previously from Gal4 enhancer-trap labels viewed by light microscopy (Tanaka et al., 2012), provides assurance that both methods reliably succeed in identifying cell types of glomerulus VA1v
evidence: The Discussion section validates the identification methods.

claim: Dense reconstruction ensures that all cells are detected and none can hide in the forest of others.
source: From FIB-SEM, in particular, we can be sure that all cells are detected and none can hide in the forest of others
evidence: The Discussion section explains an advantage of dense reconstruction.

claim: Most LNs are multiglomerular so their arbors in glomeruli other than VA1v still await completion.
source: On the other hand, most LNs are multiglomerular (Chou et al., 2010; Tanaka et al., 2012) so that their arbors in glomeruli other than VA1v still await completion
evidence: The Discussion section acknowledges incomplete LN reconstructions with citations.

claim: Reporter Gal4 screens may not have identified all neurons per identified class.
source: Reporter Gal4 screens may not have identified all neurons per identified class, however.
evidence: The Discussion section suggests limitations of genetic screens.

claim: Tobin et al. (2017) report three PNs on the left side of glomerulus DM6 and two on the right side.
source: In particular, from Gal4 lines Tobin et al. (2017) report three PNs on the left side glomerulus DM6 and two on the right side
evidence: The Discussion section cites specific findings from another study.

claim: A total of only 59 PN types for all 50 glomeruli have been labeled by Gal4 drivers in Tanaka et al. (2012), an average of about one PN per glomerulus.
source: whereas a total of only 59 types for all 50 glomeruli have been labeled by Gal4 drivers in another study (Tanaka et al., 2012), an average of about one PN per glomerulus.
evidence: The Discussion section cites and analyzes findings from Tanaka et al. 2012.

claim: Most glomeruli contain an average of 2 ± 1 uniglomerular PNs according to photoactivating GH146-Gal4 positive PNs.
source: In a more complete inventory revealed by photoactivating GH146-Gal4 positive PNs, most glomeruli are reported to contain an average of 2 ± 1 uniglomerular PNs
evidence: The Discussion section cites findings from a more complete inventory.

claim: Six glomeruli, including VA1v, are innervated by 6 ± 2 PNs according to Grabe et al. (2016).
source: while six remaining glomeruli, which include VA1v, are innervated by 6 ± 2 PNs (Grabe et al., 2016).
evidence: The Discussion section cites specific findings about VA1v from Grabe et al. 2016.

claim: VA1v is innervated by sensilla containing olfactory receptors involved in courtship and mating.
source: The VA1v glomerulus is innervated by sensilla containing olfactory receptors involved in courtship and mating (Grabe et al., 2016)
evidence: The Discussion section describes VA1v function with a citation.

claim: The large number of VA1v PNs is predicted to improve the detection accuracy and latency of odor stimuli.
source: The large number of VA1v PNs is a feature predicted to improve the detection accuracy and latency of odor stimuli (Jeanne and Wilson, 2015)
evidence: The Discussion section makes a functional prediction with a citation.

claim: The large number of PNs in VA1v may encode diverse stimulus features.
source: and may also encode diverse stimulus features (Grabe et al., 2016).
evidence: The Discussion section suggests a functional role with a citation.

claim: The number of PNs previously seen in genetic screens is significantly fewer than the 18 found from FIB-SEM.
source: The number of PNs previously seen in genetic screens is significantly fewer than the 18 we find from FIB-SEM
evidence: The Discussion section compares current findings with previous genetic screens.

claim: The genetic methods so far used underestimate the reported PN numbers, suggesting that GH146 Gal4 screens are far from saturated.
source: but suggest that the genetic methods so far used underestimate the reported PN numbers, and thus that GH146 Gal4 screens are far from saturated.
evidence: The Discussion section draws a conclusion about genetic screen completeness.

claim: The study was unable to annotate appositions that could be reliably interpreted as putative gap junctions between neurons.
source: As for other connectomes, in the antennal lobe (Rybak et al., 2016; Tobin et al., 2017) and optic neuropiles (Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015), we were therefore unable to annotate appositions that we could reliably interpret as putative gap junctions (Bennett and Goodenough, 1978) between neurons.
evidence: The Discussion section acknowledges a limitation with citations.

claim: ORNs express a cholinergic phenotype.
source: As single classes, the ORNs express a cholinergic phenotype (Wilson, 2013)
evidence: The Discussion section describes neurotransmitter phenotype with a citation.

claim: Projection neurons that project to the mushroom body calyx are cholinergic.
source: as do the projection neurons, at least those that project to the mushroom body calyx (Yasuyama et al., 2002)
evidence: The Discussion section describes neurotransmitter phenotype with a citation.

claim: Projection neurons that project to the lateral horn are cholinergic.
source: and lateral horn (Yasuyama et al., 2003)
evidence: The Discussion section describes neurotransmitter phenotype with a citation.

claim: LNs are likely to be either GABAergic and thus inhibitory, or glutamatergic and thus probably also inhibitory.
source: while LNs are likely to be either GABAergic (Wilson and Laurent, 2005; Okada et al., 2009 ; Seki et al., 2010), and thus inhibitory, or glutamatergic and thus probably also inhibitory (Liu and Wilson, 2013).
evidence: The Discussion section describes LN neurotransmitter phenotypes with citations.

claim: Widespread synaptic reciprocity has been identified among synaptic circuits in many different brains.
source: Widespread synaptic reciprocity has been identified among synaptic circuits in many different brains and is hardly new.
evidence: The Discussion section provides context about synaptic reciprocity.

claim: The anatomical demonstration of reciprocal synapses was reported in very early EM studies on the vertebrate olfactory bulb.
source: Indeed, the anatomical demonstration of reciprocal synapses was reported in very early EM studies, both on the vertebrate olfactory bulb (Rall et al., 1966)
evidence: The Discussion section provides historical context with a citation.

claim: Reciprocal synapses were identified among circuits of the inner retina at feedback synapses of amacrine cells.
source: and among the circuits of the inner retina, at feedback synapses of amacrine cells (Dowling and Boycott, 1966).
evidence: The Discussion section provides historical context with a citation.

claim: In the tadpole larva of Ciona, the total proportion of reciprocal synaptic connections between neuron pairs is 0.39.
source: while in the tadpole larva of Ciona the total proportion of reciprocal synaptic connections between neuron pairs is 0.39 (Ryan et al., 2016).
evidence: The Discussion section compares reciprocity with another organism with a citation.

claim: The ratio of strongly reciprocal pairs in the antennal lobe is 0.25.
source: By comparison we find a ratio of 0.25 for strongly reciprocal pairs in the antennal lobe.
evidence: The Discussion section provides the reciprocity ratio for comparison.

claim: Silencing LN1 and LN2 cells in the entire antennal lobe fails to modulate either glomerular input or output activity.
source: It is particularly telling that silencing the populous LN1 and LN2 cells in the entire antennal lobe fails to modulate either glomerular input or output activity
evidence: The Discussion section cites functional evidence.

claim: LN1 and LN2 may play a role in more local interactions, possibly on a global or longer time scale.
source: suggesting their lack of influence on odor identity coding as a whole, and their possible role instead in more local interactions, possibly on a global or longer time scale (Strube-Bloss et al., 2017)
evidence: The Discussion section makes a functional prediction with a citation.

claim: The dissected brain was from a 6 day female fruit fly, a cross between homozygous w1118 and CS wild type.
source: The dissected brain of a 6 day female fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster, a cross between homozygous w1118 and CS wild type
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the specimen.

claim: The brain was prepared by high-pressure freezing and freeze substitution.
source: was prepared by high-pressure freezing and freeze substitution as previously reported (Takemura et al., 2013).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the preparation method with a citation.

claim: An image stack of approximately 8,900 FIB-SEM images was acquired from the block face.
source: An image stack of ~8,900 FIB-SEM images was then acquired from the block face (Knott et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2017)
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides the number of images with citations.

claim: Images were collected at a resolution of 8 nm/pixel in a frontal plane from anterior to posterior.
source: collecting images from the brain's right side at a resolution of 8 nm/pixel, in a frontal plane from anterior to posterior
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes imaging parameters.

claim: A focused gallium ion beam was used to remove 2 nm from the block face between images.
source: In between images a focused gallium ion beam was used to remove 2 nm from the block face
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the milling process.

claim: Consecutive sets of four images were summed to generate 8 nm voxels that yielded an isotropic stack with 8 × 8 × 8 nm resolution.
source: Minor shifts in these were aligned using affine transforms and consecutive sets of four images summed to generate 8 nm voxels that after final alignment yielded an isotropic stack with 8 × 8 × 8 nm resolution.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes image processing.

claim: An algorithm was used to identify presynaptic organelles (T-bar ribbons) to enable large-scale automated imaging of synaptic contacts.
source: To demarcate the specific glomerulus we first used an algorithm that identified the presynaptic organelles, T-bar ribbons (Fröhlich, 1985; Hamanaka and Meinertzhagen, 2010), to enable large-scale, automated imaging of synaptic contacts (Huang and Plaza, 2014; Kreshuk et al., 2011).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the synapse detection method with citations.

claim: The algorithm generated a synapse point cloud of over 500,000 synaptic puncta for the entire antennal lobe.
source: Applied to the entire antennal lobe's FIB image stack, these generated a synapse point cloud of over 500,000 synaptic puncta (Figure 1A,B), as previously reported (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides the total number of detected synapses with a citation.

claim: Two trained proofreaders with recall proficiency exceeding 85% and precision exceeding 94.7% were used to annotate presynaptic T-bars.
source: For synapse annotation two trained proofreaders who had attained a recall proficiency in excess of 85% and a precision of >94.7% were used to annotate presynaptic T-bars in the EM volume.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the annotation process and quality metrics.

claim: A small minority of T-bars (<1%) that lacked clear PSDs were removed from the dataset.
source: A small minority of T-bars (<1%) that lacked clear PSDs were removed from the dataset.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes data curation.

claim: A total of 3822 pathways with one synaptic contact were identified and checked.
source: A total of 3822 pathways with one synaptic contact were identified. These were all checked by a second proof-reader and approximately 2881 were verified
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes quality control procedures.

claim: The analysis took 60 person months of proofreading time and 20 person months for curation.
source: Our analysis took 60 person months of proofreading time and 20 person months for curation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section quantifies the effort required.
